items.title: The US services sector is again signaling stagflation: ISM Services PMI rose +0.1 point in July, to 54.1, while the employment index dropped -3.6 points, to 47.4, the lowest reading since March and back in contraction territory. This is also the 2nd-lowest reading since October and marks the 4th monthly contraction over the last 5. At the same time, the prices paid index surged +2.6 points, to 70.3, near the highest since October 2022. Prices paid have now trended higher for over 2 years, rising +16.9 points since March 2024. In other words, the economy is increasingly under pressure from both rising prices and a weakening labor market. The threat of stagflation is intensifying.

items.title: BREAKING: Call option volume in the S&P 500 spiked to a record 4.0 million contracts on Tuesday. This figure has more than doubled over the last several weeks. By comparison, daily call option volume never exceeded 2 million contracts until Q4 2023. Furthermore, call option volume averaged ~700,000 contracts a day in 2020-2021. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 put/call skew, measuring the relative demand for downside protection versus upside exposure, posted its largest two-day decline since 2017. Risk appetite is absolutely exploding.

Overall, passive equity fund inflows have more than quadrupled since mid-2025. Passive investing remains exceptionally popular.

items.title: BREAKING: US-listed ETFs have attracted +$1.2 trillion in inflows year-to-date, the largest amount at this point of the year on record. This figure is already double the inflows recorded over the same period in 2025. This has also surpassed every full-year total in history except 2025, which saw +$1.5 trillion in inflows. At the current pace, US-listed ETFs are on track to exceed +$2.1 trillion in annual inflows for the first time, ~50% above last year's all-time high. Meanwhile, the semiconductor ETFs, $SMH and $SOXX, posted a combined +$13 billion in inflows in July, the largest monthly total on record. ETF demand is surging at an unprecedented rate.

items.title: Oil industry profits are soaring: Earnings for 5 major Western oil companies are on track to surge to ~$44 billion in Q2 2026, the 3rd-largest quarterly total on record. The only quarters with larger profits were Q2 and Q3 2022, when oil prices exceeded $120/barrel. This comes as ExxonMobil, $XOM, posted $14.7 billion in profit, its strongest quarter since Q3 2022. At the same time, Chevron, $CVX, reported a record $12.1 billion quarterly profit, surpassing its previous high set in 2022. Meanwhile, Shell, $SHEL, reported $9.8 billion in profit in Q2, its 2nd-largest quarterly profit in the company's history. Oil companies are cashing-in massive gains amid the Iran War.

items.content:
The US manufacturing recovery is accelerating:

ISM Manufacturing PMI rose +2.3 points in July, to 55.6, the highest since May 2022.

This marks the 7th consecutive monthly expansion.

Since December 2025, the index has surged +7.7 points, the biggest increase since the 2020 pandemic recovery.

This comes as new orders rose +0.7 points, to 56.7, the 3rd-highest since February 2022, pointing to further strength ahead.

At the same time, the employment index jumped +3.1 points, to 52.8, the highest since August 2022, marking the first monthly expansion since January 2025.

Meanwhile, prices paid fell -1.9 points, to 71.1, the lowest since February, posting the 3rd consecutive monthly decline by a total of -13.5 points. 

Manufacturing activity is gaining momentum.

items.title: Chinese investors are rotating back into gold: China's gold-backed ETFs have recorded 14 consecutive daily inflows ending Monday, the longest streak since March. Over this period, these funds have attracted +$1.2 billion. The largest single-day inflow during this streak totaled +$370 million. Before this rebound, China's gold-backed ETFs recorded outflows in 38 of 44 trading sessions. This comes as elevated volatility in China's stock market has renewed interest in alternative assets, particularly among institutional investors. Chinese investors are increasingly bullish on gold.

items.content:
BREAKING: US job openings dropped -178,000 in June, to 7.36 million, the lowest since March.

This marks the 2nd consecutive monthly decline, bringing the total drop to -226,000.

The decline was driven by private education and health services, as well as leisure and hospitality, which fell -133,000 and -86,000, respectively.

This was followed by wholesale trade and professional and business services, which declined -74,000 and -71,000, respectively.

Despite the decline, there are still 265,000 more available vacancies than unemployed workers, the 2nd-largest difference since January 2025.

As a result, the ratio of job openings to unemployed workers remains at 1.0, the highest since January 2025.

The labor market is becoming increasingly unstable.
— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) Aug 5, 2026
